sidebar.label: Controls
intro.title: Your city, your plan, your priorities
intro.text: Choose what matters most. We'll show where green improvements in Olomouc would best reduce heat stress for the people most affected.
presets.label: Presets
preset.balance.title: Balance
preset.balance.text: Not sure yet? Every factor counts equally.
preset.balance.explain: All three factors count the same. A good starting point if you have no strong preference.
preset.cool-street.title: Cool streets
preset.cool-street.text: Focus on the hottest, busiest places.
preset.cool-street.explain: Heat counts most. Hot places where many people live or spend the day move to the top of the list.
preset.protect-vulnerable.title: Protect vulnerable
preset.protect-vulnerable.text: Focus on older residents, young children, schools and doctors.
preset.protect-vulnerable.explain: Vulnerable groups count most. Areas with many older residents, young children, schools or doctors move to the top.
preset.pocket-parks.title: Pocket parks
preset.pocket-parks.text: Focus on people who live far from green space.
preset.pocket-parks.explain: Lack of green and vulnerable groups count most. Places where people live far from parks move to the top.
preset.quick-wins.title: Quick wins
preset.quick-wins.text: Places with high need and space to build now.
preset.quick-wins.explain: Same weights as Balance, plus "Only show places we can build" is switched on. Places with high need AND space to build move to the top.
preset.green-roofs.title: Green roofs
preset.green-roofs.explain: Not available yet. Needs building energy data, coming soon.

weights.title: Fine-tune what matters
weights.desc: Set how important each factor is. Higher weights give that factor more influence on the final score.
factor.he.info: Hot areas where many people live. Heat combines night-time heatwave temperature (45%), surface temperature (40%) and daytime maximum (15%): the urban heat island is strongest at night, when sealed surfaces release stored heat.
factor.v.info: Older residents (65+, especially 75+), young children, schools, kindergartens and doctors.
factor.gd.info: Little vegetation, tree cover or accessible green space (parks, forests, meadows), a lot of sealed ground (roofs, asphalt, concrete), or a long walk to the nearest green area. Vegetation includes courtyard and street trees seen by satellite in summer 2026.
toggle.label: Only show places we can build
toggle.help: Limits results to areas with brownfields, vacant land, public buildings, under-used car parks, cycle routes or suitable streets. Railways, main roads and water are left out.
ranking.title: Where to act first
ranking.desc: Areas with the highest need for green improvements, based on your priorities.
footer.note: Provisional results. Scores combine heatwave temperatures (night and day), surface temperature, population, vulnerable groups, green vegetation (Sentinel-2, summer 2026), tree cover, sealed ground, walking distance to parks and available land on a 200 m hexagon grid (H3). Checked against 2,091 places residents marked as comfortable or uncomfortable on hot days. This version focuses on heat stress. Use as a guide, not a final decision.
